question.problem:
Consider a vector $\textbf{a}$ and a point $O$ (shown below). Draw a vector that is equal to the vector $\textbf{a}$ and has its tail at $O.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196310/assets/571e2d2a8ffab997a13f99973a8605c5b9b410439239a3acef5a7fd1dac939ae.png)
question.worked_solution:
First, we sketch the line that is passing through $O$ and parallel to $\textbf{a}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196310/assets/1c1acea46337104f17184784dfc9fecc21360112fc510ac56665565e1c800804.png)

Now, we choose a point $B$ on the line, in the direction of $\textbf{a},$ such that $OB$ equals the length of $\textbf{a}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196310/assets/0931711b7da5d109085f729999016f0b7c7fb7930f658a909739910c37d05ce8.png)

So, the vector $\overrightarrow{OB}$ is equal to the vector $\textbf{a}$ and has its tail at $O.$
